title: Apple trained its own AI model for China with help from Alibaba
slides: Why would Apple need Alibaba to build AI?
Apple trained its China model with Alibaba's help.
The model will run locally on iPhones, not in cloud.
China users get AI without sending data abroad.
For you: wait for Chinese iPhone keynote before buying.
thread_text:
1. Why Apple chose Alibaba

Apple's China AI model is trained with Alibaba's help, not built from scratch. The partnership was confirmed by Alibaba's chairman.

2. The local processing twist

Unlike cloud-based AI, this model runs locally on iPhones. That means faster responses and no dependence on internet speed for basic features.

3. Data stays in China

All user data is processed on-device, so nothing is sent abroad. This complies with China's strict data laws while still offering AI features.

4. The consequence for privacy

Local processing reduces privacy risks but limits the model's complexity. So don't expect the same power as cloud-based assistants like ChatGPT.

5. Wait before you buy

If you're in China, hold off on a new iPhone until the keynote confirms AI features. Otherwise, you might miss out on the full experience.

instagram.caption:
Your next iPhone in China won’t send your messages to a cloud—Apple’s AI runs entirely on-device, trained with Alibaba’s help, and confirmed by Alibaba’s chairman. 🍎📱

That means faster replies and stricter data localization: nothing leaves the country, which sidesteps China’s data laws. But local processing also caps the model’s brainpower—don’t expect ChatGPT-level reasoning in Siri.

For creators, this changes how you automate captions or edit photos on-device in China—no cloud dependency, but simpler outputs.

If you’re buying an iPhone in China, will you wait for the keynote to see which features actually ship? 👀
